Let the wall temperature excess be

\[
\theta_w(x)=T_w(x)-T_\infty=\frac{C}{x},
\]

with \(T_\infty\) constant and \(C>0\) for heating. For a steady, laminar, Boussinesq natural-convection boundary layer on a vertical surface, use the self-similar form

\[
\eta=\frac{y}{a x^{1/2}},\qquad
\theta(x,y)=\frac{C}{x}F(\eta),\qquad
u(x,y)=U_0 f(\eta),
\]

where \(a\) and \(U_0\) are constants determined by the fluid properties and the similarity solution. Substitution into the momentum and energy equations balances all terms when

\[
\delta \sim x^{1/2},\qquad u_{\max}\sim x^0.
\]

Then the requested variations are:

| Quantity | Variation with \(x\) |
|---|---|
| Local wall heat flux \(q^{\prime\prime}\) | \(\displaystyle x^{-3/2}\) |
| Heat rate per unit width \(Q\) | \(\displaystyle x^{-1/2}\) up to an additive constant, depending on definition |
| Boundary-layer thickness \(\delta\) | \(\displaystyle x^{1/2}\) |
| Maximum velocity \(u_{\max}\) | \(\displaystyle x^0\) (constant) |
| Normal velocity at the edge \(v_\infty\) | \(\displaystyle x^{-1/2}\) in magnitude |

More explicitly,

\[
q^{\prime\prime}
=-k\left.\frac{\partial \theta}{\partial y}\right|_{y=0}
\propto \frac{\theta_w}{\delta}
\propto \frac{x^{-1}}{x^{1/2}}
\propto x^{-3/2}.
\]

For \(Q\), if it is interpreted as the heat carried in the boundary layer per unit width,

\[
Q \sim \int_0^\infty u\,\theta\,dy
\propto U_0\,\theta_w\,\delta
\propto x^{-1/2}.
\]

If \(Q\) is instead defined as a cumulative surface heat transfer from a finite station \(x_1\) to \(x\),

\[
Q(x)=Q(x_1)+\int_{x_1}^x q^{\prime\prime}\,dx'
\propto x_1^{-1/2}-x^{-1/2},
\]

so the variable part still has the \(x^{-1/2}\) dependence, and the total heat transferred from any finite \(x_1\) to infinity is finite.

For \(v_\infty\), using mass conservation,

\[
v_\infty=-\frac{d}{dx}\int_0^\infty u\,dy,
\]

and since \(\int_0^\infty u\,dy\sim u_{\max}\delta\propto x^{1/2}\),

\[
|v_\infty|\propto x^{-1/2}.
\]

If \(v_\infty\) is instead meant as the streamwise velocity outside the boundary layer in the quiescent ambient fluid, that velocity is zero.

Physical realizability: the exact law \(\theta_w=C/x\) is singular at the leading edge because \(\theta_w\), \(q^{\prime\prime}\), and \(v_\infty\) all become infinite as \(x\to 0\). Therefore it cannot be realized exactly on a finite, smooth surface with finite heat input at a real leading edge. It is, however, an idealized self-similar similarity flow for \(x>0\). It can arise, or be approached, if the leading edge is effectively a concentrated heat source, or if the surface is actively controlled so that its temperature decays as \(1/x\) downstream of a small localized heater. The required surface heat-flux distribution is then

\[
q^{\prime\prime}\propto x^{-3/2}.
\]

Thus the flow would occur in steady laminar natural convection with constant fluid properties, uniform ambient temperature, no significant forced flow, and a vertical surface whose leading-edge region is singular or sharply localized.
